main_text.p: demia Ordo reuerendus animaduertisset:in stis sane de caussis( ubi is legibus & censura illius cū laude satisfecisset) testimonium & gradū Doctoris Theologia orthodoxa postu-lanti, ad diē 28. Nouemb. illū libenter, ὁμο-μόνως ᾧ νομίμως, me Hierophāta & Designa-tore, σὺ Θεῷ, εἰ conferre, decreuit. Amater itaq; & officiosè ad Panegyrè hanc Doctura Theologica inuito, & meo, & clarissimorum Collegarū meorū nomine, omniū Professio-nū Doctores & Professores celeberrimos: flo-rente stemmatū, virtutū & erudita doctri-na laude, Nobilitate; cæterosq; pietatis & o-ptimarū artiū & disciplinarū studiosos: ac illud etiā atq; etiam peto, vt vnā nobiscum summum & vnicum nostrum Doctorem Ie-sum Christum(cui vero & æterno Deo,sicut Patri æterno & Spiritui Sancto adorationis & gratiarum actionis cultum debet tota or-thodoxa & catholica Ecclesia) comprecetur, vt pro sua immensa bonitate non solum huic nostro instituto sed etiam toti nostro Ministe-rio benedicat, efficiatq; vt cum omni mode-stia, etiam in medijs lachrymis & tentatio-nib seruiamus ipsi per omne nostram vitam. Ne autē ἀσύμβολον[?] sit in [?]Actu solenni

page.notes: Greek in the line "ὁμο-/μόνως ᾧ νομίμως" and "σὺ Θεῷ, εἰ" is transcribed as far as legible; the Greek ligature after "ἀσύμβολ" is uncertain. A sign stands before "Actu" and is not transcribed. The initial "stis" on the second line is partly lost and uncertain. The mark "N 4" at the foot is the gathering signature, and "hic" at the right is the catchword.
